summary: This breakdown details the tickets required to implement the minimal Notes CRUD MVP using Python FastAPI, SQLite, and a vanilla JavaScript frontend. It covers specification design for UI/UX and Backend, backend implementation with pytest tests, frontend single-page UI implementation, and full QA verification.

tickets.title: Design single-page Web UI for Notes app
tickets.description: Create design spec detailing HTML/CSS layout, wireframes, component states (loading, empty, error), form controls, and delete confirmation modal/flow.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec defines layout for single page index.html with vanilla JS (no framework or build step).
Includes state specs for note list, search input with title filtering, create/edit form, and delete button with confirmation dialog.
Defines UI representation for loading, empty ('No notes yet'), and error states.

tickets.title: Define OpenAPI spec and database schema for Notes API
tickets.description: Write OpenAPI spec and SQLite/SQLAlchemy schema specification for Notes CRUD operations and validation rules.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAPI schema defines endpoints POST /notes, GET /notes (with ?q= query filter), GET /notes/{id}, PUT /notes/{id}, DELETE /notes/{id}.
DB schema defines Note entity: id (auto-increment int), title (1-120 chars), content (optional, max 5000 chars), created_at and updated_at (ISO-8601).
Specifies response schemas, HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204, 404, 422), and validation error responses.

tickets.title: Implement FastAPI backend and SQLite database for Notes CRUD
tickets.description: Build FastAPI application, SQLAlchemy models, database setup, and API routes per the OpenAPI and DB specs.
acceptance_criteria: FastAPI app serves POST /notes, GET /notes (sorted newest first, with case-insensitive ?q= title filter), GET /notes/{id}, PUT /notes/{id}, and DELETE /notes/{id}.
Data persistence uses SQLite via SQLAlchemy with specified field constraints (title 1-120 chars, content max 5000 chars).
Returns 404 for non-existent notes on GET, PUT, DELETE, and 422 for validation errors.
Includes pytest test suite covering all endpoints, 404 scenarios, title search, and validation error cases.

tickets.title: Implement single-page web UI with vanilla JS
tickets.description: Develop index.html and vanilla JavaScript logic to interface with the Notes API for search, list display, creation, editing, and deletion.
acceptance_criteria: index.html and vanilla JS implement list view with search box filtering notes by title.
Form enables creating new notes and editing existing notes.
Delete action triggers confirmation before calling DELETE endpoint.
UI handles and displays loading indicator, empty state ('No notes yet'), and error messages appropriately.
No frontend frameworks or build tools are used.

tickets.title: QA verification of Backend Notes API and pytest suite
tickets.description: Verify all FastAPI REST endpoints, status codes, query filtering, database constraints, validation errors, and execute pytest suite.
acceptance_criteria: All API endpoints pass functional verification: POST (201), GET list (200), GET single (200/404), PUT (200/404), DELETE (204/404).
Case-insensitive title search ?q= returns correct filtered list sorted newest first.
Validation constraints (title 1-120 chars, content max 5000 chars) return 422.
Pytest test suite executes cleanly with 100% endpoint coverage.

tickets.title: QA verification of Frontend UI and End-to-End Notes workflows
tickets.description: Test single-page UI interaction with API, search box behavior, create/edit/delete flows, delete confirmation dialog, loading, empty, and error states.
acceptance_criteria: Verified search box filters notes dynamically or on submission.
Verified create note, edit note, and delete note (with confirmation dialog) update state correctly in UI and database.
Verified empty state ('No notes yet'), loading state, and backend error states render properly.
